references.note: One unreviewed post (2026-09-11) on the growth of lcm(n!-1); nothing on fractional parts of the finite sums.

summary: No proof of this statement is known. With F_N = sum_{n=2}^N N!/(n!-1), it asks that for arbitrarily large N the fractional part of F_N stay out of the open window (1-1/N, 1-1/(N+1)). It implies the irrationality of sum_{n>=2} 1/(n!-1) (Erdős problem 68) through erdos-68--h1 and erdos-68--h5, and it is implied by erdos-68--h3 (whose window [1-2/N, 1) contains this one), so it is the weaker of the two open cores. If S = p/q, the fractional part equals 1 - c_N for every N >= max(q, 4), where c_N = N!·sum_{n>N} 1/(n!-1) lies in the window; irrationality excludes only that one point. No result on the distribution of these fractional parts is known to us.
